significance.justification: A verified-true result would establish that an LLM has a "graded epistemic strength" direction distinct from truth, that mismatch between decoded strength and answer confidence predicts belief-versus-knowledge errors, and that intervening on this direction changes assertion strength and selective-prediction reliability without changing factual judgment; this combines a form-(ii) causal mechanism with a form-(iii) predictive coupling between measurable quantities. It would establish both a behavioral phenomenon and an internal mechanism, constraining expectations about which items will be overasserted or overhedged rather than merely showing that confidence is represented; this matters because uncertainty measures such as P(True) in Kadavath et al. and semantic uncertainty in Kuhn et al. are already used to predict model errors. The claim is determinate, and a negative result would specifically rule out a separable graded-strength representation and its miscalibration as the explanation for belief-versus-knowledge confusion, although it would not rule out other confidence mechanisms. Topic-substitution check: deleting the monotone axis, confidence-mismatch coupling, and content-preserving causal intervention leaves only generic research on LLM beliefs, which would not earn this score.

reach.justification: The concrete handles are the "decoded internal strength" predictor, the "strength direction" intervention, and the proposed alignment of strength to accuracy for selective prediction. The predictor is ex ante because it can flag likely errors before correctness is observed, while steering supplies an action window by making the model hedge or assert before producing the consequential response; the intended downstream users therefore include model auditors and practitioners implementing abstention or risk-coverage policies, not only mechanistic-interpretability researchers. After per-model re-extraction, the claimed strength–accuracy mismatch still predicts what should be found and calibrated steering should improve reliability, so part of the conclusion transfers as a relation rather than merely as a search procedure, though the stated possibility that "effects may vary across model families and scale" limits universal uptake. Topic-substitution check: the topic alone supplies neither this ex-ante predictor nor the calibration intervention, so the reach score comes from the claim-specific handles rather than from the general importance of studying beliefs.
